The Frequency of Salt

Elias preferred the heavy silence of the 2026 November coast, until the static on his workbench radio began to breathe.

The Old Needle lighthouse had been submerged in the trench for thirty years, yet its frequency remained stubbornly, impossibly active.

Every night, a voice thin as wet parchment repeated the same cryptic assurance: the light still holds.

He felt a strange pull toward the cliffside, a phantom weight in his lungs that tasted of salt and ancient pressure.

The radio crackled once more, no longer broadcasting static, but the unmistakable sound of Elias’s own voice calling from the abyss.

He looked down as his skin hardened into granite, whispering 'the light still holds' as his kitchen flooded with freezing, deep-trench brine.
